authority: Direct user correction: sell the company/product, remove synthetic-test and demo framing
scope: Product positioning and planned first-user acquisition. No traction, numerical benefit or deployment claim.

variants.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Create ONE premium 16:9 landscape investor pitch slide for a COMPANY named AdaptOps. Full-bleed slide only, not a browser, device mockup or canvas frame.
This is a sales/company pitch. It must sell the product and business value, NOT report on a hackathon build, prototype, evaluation or implementation status.
IMPORTANT CORRECTION FROM THE USER: no synthetic data test, no demo disclaimer, no test costs, no benchmark, no A/B order example, no prototype label, no build-status panel. Those do not belong on this pitch slide. Do not replace them with fabricated traction, savings, revenue, customers or measured impact.

Received brand:
"AdaptOps"
Received tagline:
"Adapt as fast as your market changes."
Product promise:
"Your business, understood. Your next response, ready."
Short product explanation:
"An agent that connects market changes to your business, coordinates a response and executes approved actions."

Core vision:
AdaptOps knows authorised company context and prior knowledge. It follows the industry's environment, connects developments to company dependencies, risks and opportunities, prepares one shared plan across procurement, operations, sales and finance, executes approved actions in connected systems within rights, verifies results and updates company knowledge. The user opens an ALREADY PREPARED COMPANY BRIEF, not a blank chat or a watch configuration. The first market is multi-site timber and materials companies, with operations/procurement leaders as first users. The broader ambition is company adaptation, not just inventory alerts. Present this as a clear company proposition without asserting unverified deployment, customer outcomes or integrations as observed facts.

All required content must be readable on this SINGLE slide. Exact concise copy:
Brand: "AdaptOps"
Main headline: "Adapt as fast as your market changes."
Supporting pitch: "An agent that connects market changes to your business, coordinates a response and executes approved actions."
Product scene or value-area labels:
"Your next response is ready"
"Know your business"
"Spot risks and opportunities"
"Coordinate the plan"
"Approve and act"
"Verify and adapt"
One concise value line:
"Protect customer commitments. Capture new demand. Keep teams aligned."

The product scene should make a ready brief and shared action plan tangible, using only a FEW meaningful UI lines:
"Company brief"
"What changed"
"What it means for us"
"Recommended response"
"Procurement   Operations   Sales   Finance"
"Review & approve"
Do not fill the slide with duplicated labels, skeleton bars or feature-card wallpaper. Select the sensible placement of these exact labels so they explain the product. A small quiet return line may connect verified actions back to company context. No technical architecture diagram.

Three concise business-pitch areas:
"WHO IT'S FOR"
"Operations and procurement leaders in multi-site timber and materials businesses."
"WHY NOW"
"Agents can now combine live research, business context and action through connected tools."
"FIRST USERS"
"Start with 3 design partners through founder introductions in French timber and materials. Expand from one workflow across their sites."
The first-user route is a proposed market-entry plan, not acquired traction. You may use a tiny "PLAN" label if needed, but do not claim signed pilots.

DESIGN:
A beautiful company pitch with clear typographic hierarchy and real breathing room. White/pale neutral background, near-black/charcoal and deep petrol teal, restrained mint accent. One refined sans-serif family, light/medium/bold hierarchy, confident brand, airy margins, crisp text. Keep it simple and commercially convincing. Main brand/headline and product value are the focal points. The three business-pitch areas must be substantial enough to read from a stage, not tiny footnotes.
NO robots, stock illustration, factory, photos, random icons, neon, glow, dense consulting tables, six equal cards, cost charts, grey placeholder paragraphs or rounded-box overload. No long body paragraphs, no false statistics, fake URLs, QR codes, logos or testimonials. English throughout. No em dash.
Include a small unambiguous A, B or C composition label at top right, visually separate from the brand.

DIRECTION A: BRAND AND BUSINESS VALUE. Label A.
A spacious asymmetric editorial composition. Left half carries AdaptOps, a beautifully balanced large tagline and the short supporting pitch. Give the business value line prominence directly below, with comfortable leading and whitespace. Right half shows ONE beautifully crafted proposed company brief titled Your next response is ready. It moves from What changed to What it means for us to Recommended response, with one shared departmental plan and a Review & approve action. Integrate the knowledge/adaptation labels as quiet context around the brief, never a wall of cards. The lower quarter is three open, well-aligned text columns for WHO IT'S FOR, WHY NOW and FIRST USERS. Avoid a footer look: these are part of the pitch. No evidence or disclaimer row.
